dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Kevin.
Good evening. Yes, hello. I am calling the storm line because I understand City Hall is closed at this hour, so I hope someone is actually listening to this one.
Somebody's listening. Yeah, the main office closes at the end of the day, but this line picks up for storm and road stuff. What's going on?

It is the water at my house. We had that snow turning to rain, Sunday into Monday, last weekend, and now it is Tuesday and the water is still sitting there. On the other hand, the snow is gone, so it cannot be the snow anymore.
Okay. Where's the house?

174 Ayrault Street, in the Historic Hill area. The apron of my driveway, where it meets the street, holds a puddle. And the puddle drains toward the garage door, not away. This is the part I cannot accept.
Toward the garage door. Okay, got it. How deep are we talking?
About up to the hubcaps of my car. I measured with my eyes, you understand, not with a ruler. On the other hand, my car is not a large car, so perhaps you will say it is not so deep.
No, hubcap deep is plenty. That's a real puddle. Is it getting into the garage?
Not yet. It reaches the door and stops, like a dog waiting to be let in. But with another rain, I think it will come inside.

Yeah, that's the worry. [pause] Okay, writing this down. One seventy-four Ayrault, water pooled at the driveway apron, pitched toward the garage, about hubcap depth. Is there a storm drain close by, do you know?
There is a grate on the street, perhaps two houses down. I cannot say if it is blocked. I looked from my window and it is dark, so I could not see leaves or anything.
Fair enough. It's pretty dark out there now.

Yes. I do much of my looking at night, actually. I am a stargazer. I have a telescope pointed out the window of the upstairs room, and that is how I saw the water shining under the streetlight when I was looking for something far more distant.
Okay. Well, not the target you were hoping for. Has it been like this before, or is this new?

It is not new. Every time we have heavy rain, the same puddle. Nobody has fixed it. I have lived here many years and the city seems to treat it as the weather's problem. On the other hand, the street is the city's, so I think it is the city's problem.

I hear you. I don't see an earlier ticket from this address in front of me, so I'll start a fresh one and note that it's a repeat spot for you. Crews have been stretched since the storm, so I can't give you a time.
Of course. But I would like to be told something. Not silence. I have waited in silence before and it did not produce results.
Understood. Let me get a number for you. Is it the one ending in zero one eight zero?
Yes, that is the cell. Four zero one, five five five, zero one eight zero. Please do ask for Brendan McCarthy.
Brendan McCarthy, M-c-C-a-r-t-h-y, right?
Correct. Two Cs, one after the M and one at the start of the Carthy. Everybody asks.

Got it. So I'll send this to the crew that handles drainage. They'll look at the grate and at the apron. If it's a city drain issue they'll deal with it, and if it's more about how your driveway meets the street, they'll tell you what the next step is.
On the other hand, I do not wish to be sent from one office to another like a parcel. If it is the street, it is the street.
Fair. I'll put that in the notes, that you want a straight answer on whose it is.
Thank you. And please, when it is done, I would like a call back. Not before, when it is only planned. When it is done.
Call back when the work is done. Noted, and I'll underline it. Anything else, any other spots on your street?
Only this one. I have seen water at the corner as well, but that is another matter and I cannot say it is worse. I mention it only for completeness.
Okay, I'll add a line about the corner too. If it gets up over the door sill tonight, or you see the drain overflowing, call back on this line. Somebody's here till late.
I will. Thank you, Kevin. Good night.
Good night, Mr. McCarthy. Hope the sky clears up for you.
